info.text:
Paying only the minimum on a $5,000 credit card balance at 22% APR can take 19 years and cost about $8,100 in interest. This guide walks through paying off credit card debt step by step: listing every card, avoiding late-payment penalties, freezing one fixed payment, choosing between the avalanche and snowball methods, and the ways people lower their rate, from balance transfers and personal loans to nonprofit debt management plans. Worked examples show the exact math, plus what the September 2026 Fed rate hike means for card APRs and the most common mistakes.

0:00 Intro
0:38 Why the minimum is a trap
1:58 List it and stop the bleeding
3:04 Pick one fixed payment
4:11 Avalanche or snowball?
5:38 Lower the rate
7:53 Mistakes and the checklist

Sources: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Household Debt and Credit Report (Q2 2026, Aug 11, 2026; earlier Q4 reports 2019-2025); Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit (Sept 8, 2026); Federal Reserve FOMC statement (Sept 16, 2026); Credit CARD Act of 2009 and Regulation Z (12 CFR 1026.53, 1026.55); CFPB on balance transfer fees and credit counseling; FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule (2010); NFCC and NCOA on debt management plans; myFICO.

News and education, not financial advice.
